Question 1
?
Evaluate the following integral.
∫0π/2cos⁡(2x)cos⁡(5x)dx=
−521​
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's recall the sum and difference formulas for cosine: cos⁡(α−β)=cos⁡αcos⁡β+sin⁡αsin⁡βcos⁡(α+β)=cos⁡αcos⁡β−sin⁡αsin⁡β

Adding these equations, we get the following product-to-sum identity: cos⁡(α−β)+cos⁡(α+β)=2cos⁡αcos⁡βcos⁡αcos⁡β=12(cos⁡(α−β)+cos⁡(α+β))

Thus, we have cos⁡(2x)cos⁡(5x)=12(cos⁡(2x−5x)+cos⁡(2x+5x))=12(cos⁡(−3x)+cos⁡(7x))=12(cos⁡(3x)+cos⁡(7x)).

Substituting this into the integral gives ∫0π/2cos⁡(2x)cos⁡(5x)dx=∫0π/212cos⁡(3x)+12cos⁡(7x)dx=[16sin⁡(3x)+114sin⁡(7x)]0π/2=16(sin⁡(3π2)−sin⁡(0))+114(sin⁡(7π2)−sin⁡(0))=16(−1−0)+114(−1−0)=−521.
